Two student models with complementary behavior then learn from it, one for local consistency and one for broader structure, sharpening anomaly detection.
arxiv-2603-07542: Knapman and colleagues detect defects in magnetic systems from imaging data where thermal fluctuations wash out static contrast. Using finite-temperature micromagnetic simulations with random defects, they compute per-pixel time mean, time spread and latent entropy as inputs to U-Net masking models. The best signal depends on noise level, and robust detection demands training data matching expected noise stats. The work guides noise-robust defect-finding workflows for magnet imaging.
arxiv-2603-07842: Lando and colleagues study weighted sums of risks that have no finite mean, where a more even mix can strangely grow larger rather than steadier. Past rules for when one mix tops another rest on shape limits that fail when the true spread is unknown. The authors offer two test methods, one tuned to the worst case and one built on resampling, and prove they hold up in large samples and catch true breaks. Trial runs and an insurance test show the tests in use.
arxiv-2603-08242: Ross and colleagues forecast physiology to time intravenous-to-oral antibiotic switches. A switch shortens stays, cuts infections, and lowers costs, yet one in five English patients stay on intravenous drugs despite meeting switch criteria. Tools that learn from past choices repeat delays, so the team models vital sign trajectories with neural processes. It judges switch-readiness against guidelines, ranking patients. Outputs stay interpretable, adapt to guidelines without retraining, and leave judgment with clinicians. Tests on MIMIC-IV and UCLH pick more than twice as many patients as random choice.
arxiv-2603-08342: Wang and colleagues present PhaForce, a phase-scheduled visual-force policy for contact-rich manipulation. Contact-rich manipulation needs vision-led task meaning and closed-loop reactions to force spikes. Yet generative visuomotor policies update slowly due to latency and action chunking, underusing force for control-rate feedback. Existing force-aware methods often inject force blindly, lacking a clear mechanism to schedule when, how much, and where to apply force across phases. PhaForce coordinates slow chunk planning and fast residual correction through one contact and phase schedule.
arxiv-2603-08742: Changliang Wei and colleagues rebuild hidden neuron states and biophysical parameters from partial, noisy voltage traces. Fast-slow spiking and bursting models punish bad starting guesses, often stalling classic forward solvers. Their physics-informed network needs only short voltage windows, stays steady from uninformative starts, and covers Morris-Lecar regimes plus a respiratory model neuron.
arxiv-2603-08942: Pranav Mantini and Shishir K. Shah adapt vision-language models across domains with a geometric fix. Independently trained models are linked by a canonical transformation, and BiCLIP recovers a domain-level version from a few anchor samples. The method transforms multimodal features to sharpen cross-modal alignment, reaching state-of-the-art results on 11 standard benchmarks with a tiny parameter footprint.
arxiv-2603-09442: Rodolfo A. Rangel Hernandez and colleagues present a bismuth copper oxide sulfate as a rare spin ladder whose rungs couple ferromagnetically. Heat capacity, susceptibility, magnetization, and spin resonance data are joined by density-functional work and Wannier analysis of the superexchange paths. Quantum Monte Carlo runs then fix the exchange values. The two-leg ladder pairs ferromagnetic rungs with antiferromagnetic legs of like strength, though the leg path runs nearly twice as long.
arxiv-2603-09542: Ziyue Zhu and colleagues propose NS-VLA, a neuro-symbolic framework for vision-language-action models that guide robot manipulation. Today's VLA models have structure-blind backbones, weak generalization past the backbone, and flat single-objective training. NS-VLA adds a neuro-symbolic encoder that infers primitives under a plan. A solver then sets the policy by the active primitive, and joint training matches reward detail to task level. It beats prior methods in one-shot and perturbed tests, with stronger zero-shot generalization.
arxiv-2603-10142: Marcelo L. Pereira Junior and coauthors use density functional theory to study fullerene networks with atoms trapped inside their cages. The two dimensional quasi hexagonal fullerene phase was recently synthesised and holds a semiconducting backbone. Placing nitrogen, cerium or strontium inside the cages keeps that backbone while adding localised states that shift the bandgap. Absorption moves toward visible light, and lower loading levels preserve the effect.
arxiv-2603-10242: Wang presents ACE Runtime, a ZKP native blockchain layer aimed at sub second cryptographic finality. Per transaction signature checks scale in a linear way and strain hardware, so the design swaps them for light HMAC attestations in the hot path. One joined proof per block is then made off the main path, giving hard finality from proof checks and soft finality from BFT voting. Formal arguments cover unforgeability and irreversibility under standard cryptographic rules.
arxiv-2603-10742: Simon Roth presents a grammar for machine learning workflows that rejects data leakage at call time, by construction. Leakage has been found in hundreds of published papers across many fields, not for lack of textbook knowledge, but because tools do not enforce it. His grammar has eight typed primitives joined in a graph under four hard constraints, making the worst leakage types unrepresentable in its scope. A terminal assessment gate enforces the evaluate boundary at call time, with a specification precise enough to reimplement in Python or R.
arxiv-2603-10842: Yuzhi Liang and co-authors propose PivotAttack, an efficient method for hard-label text attacks that works inside-out rather than outside-in. Existing hard-label attacks wander vast search spaces inefficiently. PivotAttack uses a multi-armed bandit algorithm to find pivot sets, groups of tokens acting as prediction anchors, then perturbs them to flip the predicted label. The approach captures dependencies between words and keeps query costs low. Across traditional models and large language models, it beats top baselines in attack success rate and query efficiency.
arxiv-2603-10942: Abdallah Daddi-Moussa-Ider reviews analytic methods for slow fluid flow in wedge-shaped geometries. This setting matters for microfluidic devices and transport near corners. The article focuses on solving the Stokes equations. It solves them for a point force and a point torque. It uses the Papkovich-Neuber representation, built from four harmonic functions. It walks through the Fourier-Kontorovich-Lebedev transform method and its key steps. The work offers a framework for predicting particle motion in wedge confinement. It also helps with designing cornered microfluidic systems.
arxiv-2603-11542: Islam proposes ReHARK, a training-free framework for adapting vision-language models from one shot per class. Cache-based methods act like local estimators, with boundary bias and weak global structure. ReHARK instead frames adaptation as global proximal regularization inside a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. Its pipeline fuses CLIP and GPT-3 text knowledge with visual prototypes, then bridges the two sides with built samples. Test features get aligned to the support set, and multi-scale RBF kernels read the geometry across 11 benchmarks.
arxiv-2603-11742: Ilkiewicz and co-authors show that bow shocks around cataclysmic variables have two layers, not one bright arc. Wind theory instead predicts an inner terminal shock and an outer forward shock, split by a hot, thin cavity. Archival ultraviolet, optical, and infrared images cover three systems, including BZ Cam and V341 Ara. In each, the known bright arc is the compact inner shock, glowing in H-alpha and [OIII]. A wider infrared arc marks the forward shock's sweep-up boundary, reported here for the first time.
arxiv-2603-11842: Jarzębowicz and co-authors review the reviews: they gather secondary studies and research agendas on generative AI in information systems. From Scopus, Web of Science, and eAIS, they screen down to 28 papers from 2023 onward, then map and theme them. Generative AI promises productivity, faster innovation, personal services, and wider access to expertise, they find. Adoption is held back by shaky reliability, social and ethical risks, and a governance gap. Their agenda urges IS research to move past charting impacts.
arxiv-2603-12042: Guo, Huang, and Chen built RASP, a simulation package for MOSFET reliability rooted in first principles. As transistors shrink, defect-driven wear matters more for logic, memory, and power devices. Older models track just two or four defect configurations in the gate dielectric. RASP instead uses an all-state model that covers every configuration and the paths between them. Fed with ab initio defect data, it simulates threshold voltage shifts. Runs show oxygen vacancies drive a real share of bias temperature instability.
arxiv-2603-12242: Delepine and Yebra test the factorization habit in neutrino physics with a full S-matrix treatment. Standard work treats production, travel, and detection as free-standing steps and multiplies their probabilities. Their approach handles pion decay, propagation, and nucleon interaction as one coherent quantum process. Non-factorizable terms appear from spin and angular links between the end states. In the standard channel they shift the energy spectrum by about one percent. In the Majorana channel an azimuthal pattern offers a direct route to phases that factorized methods hide.
arxiv-2603-12642: Kwanghee Choi and co-authors probe how self-supervised speech models pack phonetic context into a single frame. Prior work showed that traits of one phone, like voicing, sit superposed in its vector. The team argues that traits of nearby phones are superposed there too, split by relative position. They find that position subspaces are near orthogonal to each other. Implicit phonetic boundaries also emerge from this structure. The findings sharpen what contextualized means for speech models.
arxiv-2603-12842: Zunzhi You and co-authors teach quadrupedal robots to turn smoothly while running at speed. Rescue and inspection work needs fast, agile movement through changing goals. Older policies learn to reach one goal and stop, so they waste momentum at each switch. Their SmoothTurn frames the task as sequential local navigation. A new reward, a lookahead window on future goals, and a goal curriculum drive learning. The trained policy ran on real robots and turned across goals with ease.
arxiv-2603-13042: Yiqi Zhou and co-authors present OpenACMv2, a framework for accuracy-constrained design of approximate digital compute-in-memory chips. Approximation can save power and area, but coupled design choices make tuning hard. Their two-level scheme searches architectures first, with a graph network surrogate for speed. Transistor sizing then runs with variation-aware Monte Carlo checks. Most of the gain came from the architecture level, with roughly 50% PDP reduction. Circuit sizing added a smaller gain while holding accuracy.
arxiv-2603-13142: Martin Sulzmann shows that critical sections in lock-based programs need not belong to a single thread. The standard lock set method assumes that a section stays inside the thread that took its locks. That assumption fails for general C and Pthread executions, he demonstrates. With a trace model of such programs, he defines critical sections with no per-thread limit. Multi-thread sections then arise in a natural way in real code. The result closes a semantic gap in the standard method.
arxiv-2603-13742: Ruiyuan Huang, Zicheng Lyu, Xiaoyi Zhu, and Zengfeng Huang study stochastic bandits under joint space and adaptivity constraints. The learner interacts in B batches and holds only W bits of persistent memory. Each constraint alone is mild, with near-minimax regret achievable under either one, prior work shows. Together they bite: any W-bit memory algorithm needs at least on the order of K over W batches for near-minimax regret. The proof rests on an information bottleneck and a localized change-of-measure lemma.
arxiv-2603-14142: Maciala, Araújo, and Patrício derive generalized inverses for matrices tied to double star digraphs. They give explicit block formulas for core, dual core, core EP, and dual core EP inverses. Existence tests come as algebraic criteria read off the block structure. Other combined outer inverses, mixing Moore-Penrose and core-type parts, are derived with their own existence rules. The results turn abstract inverse questions for this matrix class into checks that can be computed directly.
arxiv-2603-14442: Lupascu, Li and Schäfer test invertible neural networks for power grid frequency forecasts. Grid frequency shows how stable a power system is. Plain Koopman autoencoders can warp the hidden space and hurt forecasts. The team trains several invertible designs on simulated data and adds fixes for known limits. They report that coupling-layer networks work best on their own. Hybrid setups help only when paired with the right design.
arxiv-2603-14742: Xu and Boyd turn pump walk-off in downconversion from a flaw into an OAM design tool. Spontaneous parametric downconversion reliably yields orbital angular momentum entanglement. Pump walk-off breaks the rotational symmetry of the setup in practice. Total OAM conservation then fails, and state fidelity drops. The authors derive a scaling law for the OAM spread versus walk-off angle. That law shows how far the violation grows with angle. Walk-off can also shape the output state on purpose. Guidelines for lab state crafting close the study.
arxiv-2603-15242: Habibi and co-authors present SliceMapper, an app that places O-RAN network units onto cloud sites in 6G networks. The mapping of centralized and distributed units for each slice is framed as a sequential decision problem. They solve it with Q-learning in four flavors: on-policy and off-policy, each in tabular and function approximation form. Simulations across scenarios compare all four. On-policy function approximation was the most stable, with the lowest spread across seeds. The tabular variants earned higher average rewards, at 5.42 and 5.12.
arxiv-2603-15342: Takeuchi recasts cosmic structure formation as an optimal transport problem, measured with the Wasserstein distance. Power spectra and correlation functions describe clump sizes, but not how matter itself moves. His framework maps the path from the early smooth density field to a galaxy catalog in stages. In the small-fluctuation limit, the distance splits into three parts. Gravity moves mass, galaxy formation adds bias, and discrete sampling adds shot noise. The split links clustering data to real matter displacements and to baryon acoustic oscillation smearing.
arxiv-2603-15542: Shi and co-authors present InterveneBench, a benchmark for intervention reasoning in real social systems. Social science causal work needs end-to-end research design around actual policy moves. Each task grows out of a peer-reviewed study and asks for design choices and identification logic, with no causal graph given. The set holds 744 studies across many policy areas. Top language models struggle on it. Their multi-agent framework, STRIDES, improves scores a lot over leading reasoning models.
arxiv-2603-15642: Mody and co-authors present CraniMem, a memory design for long-running language model agents. Many agent memory stores act like loose databases with ad hoc rules. That habit brings unstable retention and weak consolidation. CraniMem gates writes by goals and tags items by utility. A bounded short-term buffer holds recent turns. A knowledge graph holds durable facts. A replay loop moves high-value traces into the graph and prunes weak ones. Tests show smaller drops under noise than RAG and Mem0 baselines.
arxiv-2603-15942: Douçot gives a math reading of dualities among Argyres-Douglas theories. Type A dualities from recent physics work lacked a unified math frame. Wild nonabelian Hodge theory turns theory data into singularity data. The data live on irregular connections over the projective line. Two basic moves then generate all the dualities at hand. One move is the Fourier transform on connections. The other is a Möbius swap of zero and infinity. Mirror quivers match special Hodge diagrams with no negative edges.
arxiv-2603-16042: Qiu, Mei, and Zhang free mirror descent from plain Lipschitz demands. Smoothness rules most convergence proofs through the descent lemma. Many tricks, like reshuffling and momentum, need gradient Lipschitz bounds too. Relative smoothness alone leaves those tricks unproven so far. Their dual kernel conditioning tames local kernel curvature. Paired with relative smoothness, it yields dual-space Lipschitz control. Popular kernels pass the new condition with room to spare. First complexity bounds for reshuffling mirror descent follow. Iterate convergence lands for constrained nonconvex problems as well.
arxiv-2603-16242: Kayaalp and Szehr study signal recovery from samples in two domains at once. One set of samples comes from the signal, the other from its Fourier transform. This two-sided setup helps when one domain alone gives too little data. They frame the task in finite spaces and in kernel Hilbert spaces. Tests with sinc and Hermite schemes show better conditioned systems. A spectrum monitoring example shows the same gain.
arxiv-2603-16342: Andrade and co-authors guard large IoT networks with two deep learning detectors. Connected devices ease daily life but open fresh attack paths. One proposed system uses a convolutional network, the other a memory-based LSTM. Both sort threats as binary, grouped, or multi-class cases. Tests used the CICIoT2023 dataset. Accuracy topped 99% for binary and grouped sorting. Multi-class scores reached 98.6% or better.
arxiv-2603-16742: Xu and co-authors let roadside sensors teach self-driving cars, with no labels at all. Roadside units watch fixed spots and see the same scenes repeatedly. They learn local 3D detectors from unlabeled data on their own. Their predictions stream to passing cars as pseudo-labels. The cars train a standalone detector from that supervision. At test time no roadside help is needed. In CARLA tests, the pipeline reached 82.3% AP on vehicles. That nears a fully supervised upper bound.
arxiv-2603-16942: Kim and co-authors present UNICORN, a method for ultrasound Nakagami imaging of fatty liver disease. Nakagami imaging can quantify tissue scattering, but window size choice and estimator instability blur results. UNICORN gives a closed form, pixel by pixel estimator based on the score function of the ultrasound envelope signal. It maps the full field rather than fixed windows over small regions. In tests on real patient envelope data, the authors report clear visual distinction of steatosis related scattering. They also report robustness and generalizability across experiments.
arxiv-2603-17142: Olesen Recke and Hansen study whether the drift of a dynamical system can be recovered from its steady state distribution. Their setting is Lyapunov models: steady states of a linear stochastic equation whose drift follows a directed graph. They derive equations for the cumulant tensors of all orders. Under a non Gaussianity assumption, they prove the drift matrix is generically identifiable for any connected graph. They propose an estimator and derive its large sample behavior. Simulations confirm the result, but show accuracy only at large sample sizes.
arxiv-2603-17342: Jo sets out a quantum algorithm for non-Hermitian linear response, a tool for studying open quantum systems. The method turns non-unitary correlation functions into a unitary form that quantum hardware can run. It uses Schrödingerization inside an expanded Liouville space. Tests with a noise model of a 133-qubit device keep key spectral features intact, he reports. The approach avoids mid-circuit steps that break unitarity, so standard error fixes still apply.
arxiv-2603-17442: Jeong and co-authors describe the data pipeline for the KMTNet Synoptic Survey of the Southern Sky. The pipeline checks image quality, solves astrometry, masks bad pixels, and stacks frames. Two-stage photometric calibration ties zero points to APASS, SkyMapper, and Gaia data. The release covers over 4,000 square degrees at 22 to 23 magnitude depth. Difference imaging on the stacks found transients in real time, they report, including gravitational-wave follow-ups.
arxiv-2603-17542: Gupta, Kaplan, Lindermayr, Schlöter, and Yingchareonthawornchai simplify a scheduling optimality proof. The setting is epsilon-clairvoyant flow time scheduling, where job sizes are known only roughly in advance. Flow time counts how long each job spends in the system overall. The algorithm under study is Shortest Lower-Bound First, from their earlier work. Their new analysis proves its optimality with a cleaner argument. The result tightens theory for scheduling under partial foresight.
arxiv-2603-17742: Hassan and Rasanen study cosmic inflation with a Gauss-Bonnet term in Palatini gravity. In this frame the term is not a mere total derivative, unlike the metric frame. They solve for the connection exactly in flat FLRW space and by graded approximations beyond it. Three cases cover free, torsion-free, and metric-compatible connections. Each shifts the inflaton kinetic term like a Chern-Simons term with flipped sign, they find. Gaps from the metric frame stay small.
arxiv-2603-17842: Conselice, Copeland, and Sevillano Muñoz revive the Tolman volume test for cosmology. The classic test counts galaxies per volume across redshift to pin cosmic parameters. Galaxy evolution once made that tracing too murky to trust. Known star formation and merger histories now clean the signal, they argue. With one to ten percent accuracy on those histories, the test could rival supernova and CMB methods. Dark energy dynamics are the prize measurement.
arxiv-2603-17942: Goel, Gagrani, Lee, and Lott draw multi-token prediction out of frozen language models. Their ESP method probes the model with mask tokens built from its own embeddings. A speculative tree grows from top candidate continuations, then a light rule prunes it. Parallel checks keep decoding lossless while model calls drop. Acceptance length rose 7 to 11 percent over a strong baseline on LLaMA3, they report. Throughput gains reached 19 percent.
arxiv-2603-18042: Verma and co-authors add intuitionistic fuzzy logic to U-Net and U-Net++ for MRI brain image segmentation. Standard nets struggle with vague, imprecise image data and fuzzy tissue borders. Their IFS U-Net and IFS U-Net++ take fuzzy inputs to handle that doubt. Tests run on the IBSR and OASIS brain datasets. Scores for accuracy, Dice, and IoU improve across both sets, they report.
arxiv-2603-18242: Jo and co-authors simulate nuclear star cluster growth in a dwarf galaxy with Enzo-Abyss. Their code joins hydrodynamics with a direct N-body solver in a live galaxy. Four runs vary supernova feedback, star formation efficiency, and gas content. Both cluster mergers and in-situ star formation seem to add mass at like rates. Mergers also disrupt dense gas clumps, which suppresses in-situ formation when they occur.
arxiv-2603-18442: Banda and co-authors summarize integration techniques for worldline integrals in quantum field theory. The worldline formalism packs many Feynman diagrams into compact integral forms. Those integrals are non-standard, and standard math algorithms help little with them. The review covers the state of the art through examples from QED. Vacuum cases and constant external field cases anchor the survey.
arxiv-2603-18642: Song tests model-free policy learning on blackjack with an exact oracle as ground truth. Fixed Vegas rules define 4,600 decision cells with masked actions. Dynamic programming gives true action values and an expected value of minus 0.00161 per hand. Masked REINFORCE, SPSA, and the cross-entropy method train by simulation. REINFORCE learns fastest, matching 46.37 percent of optimal actions after one million hands. All three still show large regret in rare cells. Song also proves that bet sizing without counting collapses to the table minimum.
arxiv-2603-18742: Su and co-authors cut the cost of video diffusion models with mixed-precision quantization at inference time. Static bit widths ignore how hard each timestep is to quantize. A block's input-output gap tracks the sensitivity of its inner layers, they find. A light predictor assigns 4-bit formats to stable layers and keeps 8-bit for volatile ones. A temporal delta cache also skips blocks that barely change across steps. The combined method speeds end-to-end runs by 1.92 times and cuts memory by 3.32 times in their tests.
arxiv-2603-18842: Facciotti, Mazzocco, and Nikolaev build a category-based frame for decorated character varieties. Surfaces with boundary carry groupoid representations into GLn(C). Without marked points, these spaces match local systems and monodromy data. Marked points capture irregular singularities and lead to decorated Betti moduli spaces. Many authors have built versions of these spaces, but how they coincide was unclear. The new frame defines the spaces in one system, even with higher order poles. It is built to specialize to each known viewpoint in the literature.
arxiv-2603-19242: Gselmann and co-authors solve functional equations that add a fixed twist to the classic Cauchy form. The twist is a biadditive map, or in some cases a term built from unknown functions. They sort the solutions under varied shape and smoothness rules. Many solutions shrink to additive functions or exponential polynomials. For Levi-Civita type cases, they write the solutions in explicit form. They also state when real-valued solutions exist. Open cases that resist these methods close the work.
arxiv-2603-19542: Zhao and co-authors run direct numerical simulations of turbulence at ice-ocean boundaries. Heat and freshwater flow there sets glacier and iceberg melt rates. The runs use realistic salt diffusivity, key for the thin salt boundary layer. They vary temperature, salinity, stratification, flow speed, and slope angle. Melt rates and interface temperatures match lab measurements. Without outside flow, convection rules even at near-flat slopes. Shear matters only above background speeds of about 5 centimetres per second.
arxiv-2603-19742: Jantsch and co-authors introduce Layer-wise Target Propagation, a fast way to credit transformer parts. Dense attribution for large language models is usually far too costly. Their method works on the frozen model in one forward and one backward pass. It needs no counterfactual examples. A target vector is pushed through linearized paths in the network. That yields an effective representation at each residual position. The cost stays flat as the number of components grows. Benchmark tests showed top faithfulness with unmatched speed.
arxiv-2603-19842: Dacko and Oussi study the vacuum distribution of partial sums of nonsymmetric position operators. The operators depend on a real parameter and act on a discrete Fock space. The work sits inside V-monotone independence, a noncommutative probability setting. They work out the moments of the distribution through combinatorics. Using a Cauchy-Stieltjes transform, they find its exact form. It has one atom plus a continuous part. Graphs made by computer show the shape for several parameter values.
arxiv-2603-20042: Chen and co-authors benchmark large speech language models on low-resource speech recognition. Most past benchmarks stress high-resource languages, where these models already do well. Real use demands support for languages with little training data. LoASR-Bench covers 25 languages from 9 language families. It includes both Latin and non-Latin scripts for fair comparison. The tests expose limits of current speech models across these languages. The authors aim to guide deployment of such systems in truly multilingual settings.
arxiv-2603-20142: Antonio and co-authors add coronal loop data as a constraint on the standard solar field model. The potential field source surface model is fast and works well at large scales. Richer force free models capture those effects but cost far more compute. The new model lets the field bend away from the potential state near traced loops. It keeps control over divergence and force freeness through added terms. Tests used synthetic loops and a real rotation as the lower boundary.
arxiv-2603-20242: Li and co-authors clean speech with discrete tokens while keeping the system fast enough for live use. Many enhancement methods work on continuous signals, and token based ones can be slow. Their LL-SDR design uses tokens to separate speech from noise more cleanly. A variance ordered quantizer shapes that tokenization step. A latent space discriminator aligns enhanced embeddings with semantic ones. The system beat continuous baselines and matched autoregressive token methods. It needs only 40 giga operations for a ten second clip, and runs in real time.
arxiv-2603-20342: Acernese and the Virgo Collaboration set out the design of Advanced Virgo Plus for the O5 observing run. Lessons from the O4 run led the team to revise its upgrade plan. The main change tackles marginally stable recycling cavities in the interferometer. New stable cavities anchor a wider renewal of key subsystems. The program adds vacuum gear, suspensions, mirrors, and quantum noise reduction. Work proceeds in two steps toward better stability and sensitivity. The upgrades should greatly extend the detector's astrophysical reach.
arxiv-2603-20542: Sramek reports a hardware test of whether pairwise effects explain a quantum parity benchmark. Many workflows assume device noise is mostly pairwise in nature. Sramek runs a parity-structured label task on a 133-qubit IBM processor. A Möbius decomposition splits subset information into orders. The baseline run showed a triplet term of 0.726 bits. A stricter follow-up still kept 0.565 bits of triplet structure. A pairwise model matching all lower marginals predicts almost none. Pairwise-only classifiers reached 0.617 accuracy, while triplet models hit 0.910.
arxiv-2603-20642: Cacioli studies how transformer language models store magnitude. Past work clashes: some find log spacing, some linear, some digit based rings. This study applies psychophysics tools across three models and three domains. Log style geometry won in all 96 test cells. Yet behavior did not match geometry in every model. One model showed a human like Weber fraction, the other did not. Early layers drove magnitude work, while later layers held the strongest geometry.
arxiv-2603-20842: Xu and co-authors build a pretrained model for causal discovery that uses weak domain knowledge. Pure data driven tools lack guidance, while strong priors cost too much. Their model takes coarse prior knowledge as a middle path. A dual source encoder decoder reads observational data with the knowledge in mind. Pretraining spans varied graphs, densities, and variable counts. A curriculum adapts the model to priors of unlike strength. Tests on in distribution, shifted, and real data beat baselines. Robustness and practical value stood out in their results.
arxiv-2603-20942: Kløvedal and co-authors present Accompanist, a runtime that makes choreographic programs fault tolerant. Services usually coordinate through an orchestrator, whose central state eases recovery. Hardware limits and security rules can rule that option out. Choreographic programming gives a global view without a center, but assumes reliable networks. Accompanist instead replays computation at run time to mask faults, which keeps programs simple. It targets the Choral language and runs as sidecars next to existing services, with a correctness proof.
arxiv-2603-21142: Chen and Chandra present AlphaAdj, a navigation framework that lets a vision-language model tune robot safety in real time. Control barrier functions filter robot motion for safety, but fixed settings can be too cautious or too lax. Their system reads the camera view and produces a bounded risk estimate. That estimate updates the barrier parameter. Speed aware caps and staleness checks handle model latency. Across static and dynamic obstacle tests, the robot stays collision free and reaches goals up to eighteen percent faster.
arxiv-2603-21642: Huang and co-authors test whether AI coding tools built on the Model Context Protocol resist prompt injection. Prompt injection tops the OWASP list for language model applications, and tool poisoning is a key delivery route. They run the first empirical study across seven widely used MCP clients, from Claude Desktop to Cursor and Langflow. They map each client's defenses, including static validation, sandboxing, warnings, and audit logging. Guardrail strength varied widely: Claude Desktop held up well, while Cursor proved open to cross-tool poisoning and hidden parameter abuse.
arxiv-2603-21742: Bellier and co-authors adapt higher dimensional automata to build controllers for concurrent systems. Higher dimensional automata extend classic automata theory, but real control uses were missing. The team starts from controllers written as interpreted Petri nets. Their method turns such a net into a working closed-loop controller. Along the way, the automata view exposes vague or conflicting specs that stay hidden in the net. They prove the approach on an industrial example, linking the controller to a virtual environment and running the loop in simulation.
arxiv-2603-21842: Viswanathan and Xing study how a trader in the Kyle model should gather information before trading. An informed trader buys costly knowledge, then trades against noise traders. Information cost is measured by entropy. The authors show that continuous signals are best, whatever the prior on the asset payoff. Many signal choices give the same ex-ante value and the same spread of posterior beliefs. A normal signal can thus be used with no loss. Costlier information or calmer noise trading shrinks the belief spread and the profit on offer.
arxiv-2603-22142: Sanz and co-authors treat the choice of ansatz as a design problem for variational quantum algorithms. Many teams still pick circuit structures by heuristic rules. A poor structure can cut expressive power and make training stall. Recent theory also links expressibility to barren plateaus. The team explores a wide set of parametrized circuits as a design space. They score each circuit on expressibility, trainability, and resource cost. The scores expose trade-offs across the set. Pareto-optimal candidates stand out, and the results clarify the expressibility-trainability tension.
arxiv-2603-22342: Morales and co-authors estimate neutrino oscillation parameters with a layered transformer. Oscillation maps encode neutrino masses and mixing angles, clues to physics past the Standard Model. Reading parameters off these maps is slow with classic likelihood or Monte Carlo tools. The team recasts the task as regression on structured maps. Their transformer models angle patterns at fixed energies and links across the full spectrum. The model also gives intervals with coverage guarantees. It matches MCMC accuracy at a fraction of the cost.
arxiv-2603-22442: Hirsch and Raab argue that crypto migration needs more than a list of assets in use. Standard bills of materials come from tools and inventories, so they lack design intent and security context. The authors adapt a scenario-based review method to derive the list from the system design itself. Each entry gains notes on context, intent, and migration needs. They show the richer list captures planning facts that inventory-based lists miss.
arxiv-2603-23142: Haq and Cabot test whether language models can pass software testing certification exams. They use ISTQB sample exams, the board that certifies human testers. Sixty multimodal models from firms and open sources take 30 exams. Each model faces over one thousand questions. Transformed questions check real conceptual grasp, not rote recall. Two models pass all certifications at the set threshold. Paid models beat open ones overall. The authors review error causes and suggest exam design changes.
arxiv-2603-23242: Julio-Batalla turns to the zero mode equation on products of closed spin manifolds. Here the field A is a real vector field on the product space. He assumes the spinor's size does not grow along the manifold. Under that condition, he proves a lower bound on the norm of A. The bound runs through the Yamabe constant and the larger factor's dimension. The estimate is sharp in even dimensions. He also proves a similar bound for a related equation with a scalar factor.
arxiv-2603-23542: Kyriakou and Pisano model a dichroic refractor that bends two wave bands at set angles. Their design rests on a two-dimensional Huygens metasurface. They treat the surface as many cells, each replaced by a resonant circuit sketch. The team test the sketch across the space of refraction angles. Realized bending then guides which angle pairs work best. A rectangular cell array can be built, they find, with its size set by the low-band diffraction limit. They trace performance flaws to weak spots in the sketch.
arxiv-2603-23642: Scepi and six co-authors simulate line-driven winds from active galactic nuclei with radiation physics. Light pressure on spectral lines should launch these winds, but X-rays over-ionize the gas. Past work leaned on self-shielding under radiation models. Their Monte Carlo runs couple radiation, ionization, and flow in many directions. Steady winds need an oddly weak X-ray flux to survive. At real flux levels, shielding flickers and winds burst out in episodes. The runs yield BAL and ultra-fast outflow marks at the right viewing angles.
arxiv-2603-23942: Li and co-authors argue that research computing lacks an adapter layer between cloud machines and daily work. Graduate researchers get virtual machines fast, but turning one into a ready GPU workspace is hard. Their open-source layer builds on k3s and Coder and is already in active use. A pipeline links GitHub to the local cluster, so a commit becomes a running workspace in under five minutes. They also define metrics for judging such layers, covering deploy time, reproducibility, onboarding, and resource use.
arxiv-2603-24142: Amante and co-authors explain why oil droplets in water pick up a negative charge. They simulate an extended decane-water interface with neural-network molecular dynamics and data-driven tools. Small clusters show almost balanced charge transfer both ways. The full interface does not. A net transfer runs from water to the oil phase, giving a small surface charge density. Large self-polarization inside each phase dominates the response. Unequal hydrogen-bond motifs at the interface give the microscopic cause, they argue.
arxiv-2603-24242: Sant and co-authors study how client language mix shapes federated training of multilingual language models. Clients differ in which languages they hold and how much data each language has. They extend the FederatedScope-LLM framework for multilingual instruction tuning. A new local early stopping rule lets clients pause and resume training by their own validation scores. Monolingual clients win for single-language skill, they find. More multilingual clients give stronger, fairer global models, with the largest gains for low-resource languages, at higher training cost.
arxiv-2603-24742: Bashir and co-authors model user trust in AI systems as an evolving dynamic, not a one-shot choice. Trust means reduced monitoring in a repeated interaction with developers, and checking their behaviour is costly. Using evolutionary game theory, they study how user trust and developer safety strategies co-evolve. Analyses span imitation dynamics, replicator equations, and reinforcement learning. Three long-run regimes appear: no adoption with unsafe AI, unsafe but widely adopted systems, or safe and widely adopted systems. Monitoring cost and institutional rules decide which regime wins.
arxiv-2603-24842: Lingampalli studies how the 2025 GENIUS Act reshaped the stablecoin economy through green reserve assets. The focus is a climate-liquidity nexus: sustainable but thinly traded assets backing high-velocity payment tokens. Using vector error correction and GARCH models on high-frequency data from 2024 to 2026, the study finds a liquidity hysteresis effect. After climate-finance shocks, green-backed stablecoins recover 5.4 times more slowly than Treasury-backed ones. The greenium paid by issuers acts as a volatility multiplier, not a safety buffer, raising systemic fragility concerns.
arxiv-2603-25042: Lee and co-authors improve online 3D scene rebuilds with per-point motion reasoning in MoRGS. Fast Gaussian splatting makes live rebuilds of moving scenes possible. But older online methods let each Gaussian drift to match pixels, not true motion, since no motion cue guides them. MoRGS adds optical flow from a few key views as a light motion signal. A learned offset field fixes gaps between projected motion and seen flow. A confidence score also marks still points, so they stop wasting updates. Tests top prior online methods.
arxiv-2603-25242: Malamud, Neidhardt, and Peller pin down when a spectral shift function can be chosen real. For pairs of contractions with a trace-class gap, a shift function on the unit circle exists, and a trace formula holds. But that function may need complex values. The trio finds conditions that force a real-valued, integrable version to exist. They treat the same question for pairs of dissipative operators. An application to dissipative Schrödinger operators closes the work. These are sharp tools for scattering and perturbation theory.
arxiv-2603-25642: Schulz, Ternes, and Woydt improve algorithms for group closeness centrality maximization. The task is to pick k vertices in a graph that minimize total distance to all others. It is NP-hard. The best exact method solves integer programs of growing size. The authors add a data reduction rule that removes variables with provably fixed distances. They also seed the solver with an approximate solution. They report speedups of 4.5 times over the prior exact method. They also prove the common greedy method can be arbitrarily poor.
arxiv-2603-26142: Song, Guo, and Lin build AI students that truly act like novices for learning-by-teaching studies. Prompted models still blurt out expert answers, which breaks the illusion. Their method uses machine unlearning to strip target knowledge from a model. The agent then relearns through teaching dialogue with a human tutor. On Python concept questions, unlearned agents answer in a more novice-like way than prompt-only ones. They recover a fair share of the lost knowledge under guided teaching. Dialogue logs show clear paths of conceptual change.
arxiv-2603-26342: Bodingbauer and co-authors describe work to turn Vampire proofs into trusted proofs in Lean. Vampire is an automated prover for first- and higher-order logic with theories. As proof checking grows in demand, users need a way to trust its output. The team outlines their ongoing effort to rebuild Vampire proofs step by step inside the Lean proof assistant. The short paper reports the state of that reconstruction work and the path toward checked, trusted results.
arxiv-2603-26642: Lima, Veras, and Silva study massless Dirac fermions moving on a surface with one localised bump. They try two bump shapes, a smooth Gaussian hill and a volcano-like form. The spinor couples to the surface shape through vielbeins and the spin connection. Numeric work finds a linear, discrete energy spectrum for the fermions when Fermi velocity is accounted for. Far from the bump the states act as free waves, since curvature fades away. Near the curved zone the wave function piles up, raising local probability density.
arxiv-2603-26742: R presents a cross-lingual audit of visual reasoning in eight vision-language models across Indian languages. Reasoning tests are usually run in English, which can hide sharp drops elsewhere. The audit moves 980 questions from MathVista, ScienceQA, and MMMU into Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Kannada, and Marathi. Accuracy falls by 9.8 to 25 points when English is swapped out. Dravidian languages lose up to 13.2 points more than Indo-Aryan ones, and chain-of-thought prompts hurt Bengali and Kannada rather than helping.
arxiv-2603-27042: Carneiro and co-authors study the memory effect of gravitational pp-waves beyond the usual polarization modes. Test particles crossed by a Gaussian pulse can keep a permanent velocity and energy shift. The authors solve the geodesic equations for several multipolar indices. Working with relative motion between two particles removes coordinate artifacts. The relative kinetic energy change scales with the fourth power of wave amplitude. Its coefficient depends on the wave's multipolar structure. The energy memory is set by the integrated tidal field of the pulse.
arxiv-2603-27242: Bonte and co-authors present PHOEG, an exact online tool for extremal graph theory. The field hunts inequalities between graph invariants amid a flood of graphs. Most tools settle for rough or probabilistic answers to stay fast. PHOEG instead embeds graphs in a 2D invariant space and builds convex hulls exactly. Hull facets spell out inequalities, and vertices mark extremal graphs. Its library holds all non-isomorphic graphs up to order ten. Users can spot conjectures and counterexamples quickly. It is also used in university coursework.
arxiv-2603-27542: Lee and co-authors match image points across many views at once. Pairwise matchers often break tracks when chained over views. MV-RoMa instead predicts dense matches from one source to many targets. Pairwise results seed the model as a geometric prior. A refiner then sharpens matches with pixel-level attention. The design avoids the full cost of cross-attention. Tests yield denser and more exact 3D reconstructions. Gains hold on hard benchmark scenes.
arxiv-2603-27942: Maeda and Okazaki benchmark vision models on Japanese scene text. Mixed scripts and vertical writing challenge most systems. Character counts dwarf the Latin alphabet. JaWildText holds 3,241 cases from 2,961 fresh photos. Annotations cover 1.12 million characters. Unique types total 3,643. Tasks span dense text questions and receipt extraction. A third task varies layout and output style. The set probes gaps multilingual benches miss.
arxiv-2603-28342: Du and co-authors present Kernel-Smith, a system that evolves fast GPU kernels with help from a trained model. An agent keeps a pool of working kernel candidates and improves them round by round, guided by compile and speed feedback. The model inside is trained on past evolution traces, so it acts as a strong local improver rather than a one-shot writer. On KernelBench their 235B model beat top commercial systems. The workflow has already fed code into production projects.
arxiv-2603-28442: Breiten, Burela, and Schulze pair shifted proper orthogonal decomposition with optimal control of transport problems. Shifted POD tracks moving fronts far better than the plain version. Their route is reduce first, then optimize on the small model. For a one-dimensional advection case, they prove the reduced problem has one solution and that an optimal control exists. Benchmarks compare the shifted method's cost against standard POD.
arxiv-2603-28742: Bairathi and Nayak study charge-dependent directed flow in symmetric nuclear collisions. They use a multiphase transport model for oxygen, copper, ruthenium, gold, and uranium collisions at 200 GeV. They track the mid-rapidity flow slope and its splitting between particles and antiparticles. At low momentum, the slope depends weakly on system size. At high momentum, it depends strongly and turns negative with nuclear mass. Baryon pairs show clear splitting that grows with system size, while meson pairs show little. Hadronic final-state effects were negligible, pointing to a partonic origin.
arxiv-2603-28842: Gantenberg and Kaplan offer a new effective theory for nucleon scattering, built with dimer fields. Past theories fail to match data near 300 MeV. They trace the block to hidden nonanalytic structure in the complex momentum plane. It links to the peak of the angular momentum barrier in low waves. They define a C-matrix whose pole structure sets the range of the theory. Adding dimer fields as real degrees of freedom accounts for those poles. Fits then stay cutoff stable up to the pion production threshold for most low waves.
arxiv-2603-29142: Fawzi and co-authors introduce REFINE, an interactive feedback system for students. Good formative feedback helps learning, but personal feedback at scale is hard. Most automated tools give static, one-way comments. REFINE runs locally on small open-source language models. One agent writes feedback grounded in teaching principles. A judge-guided loop then regenerates weak feedback. A second agent answers student follow-up questions with context-aware advice. Classroom tests in a computer science course showed better feedback quality.
arxiv-2603-29242: Zhang and co-authors present RoSE, simulations of element production in a Milky Way-mass galaxy. The simulations track enrichment star by star. Five channels supply elements, from massive stars to neutron star mergers. Elements from the same channel show similar spatial and temporal patterns. Their abundances also correlate strongly with each other. Mixed-source pairs correlate much more weakly. A simple regression on source mixtures predicts correlation strength well. Comparisons with real Milky Way data agree encouragingly.
arxiv-2603-29742: Bao and co-authors present SHIFT, a training-free attack that strips watermarks from diffusion-made images. Many watermark schemes assume the generation path can be rebuilt at check time. SHIFT breaks that link by resampling the process and bending the hidden path. The marked image and its check copy end up statistically apart. Tests on nine watermark methods show 95 to 100 percent success. Image meaning and quality stay nearly intact.
arxiv-2603-30042: Tan and co-authors present HapCompass, a wearable haptic device for robot teleoperation. Contact-rich tasks need touch feedback, but handheld buzzes carry little direction. Their low-cost device rotates one vibrating actuator to render two-dimensional directional cues. In user tests, it beats vision-only and plain vibration setups. Success rates rise, while task time and peak contact force fall. Demonstration data gathered with the device also trains better policies. The design and interface code are public.
arxiv-2604-00142: Chen and twelve colleagues run a 92-student calculus experiment with three groups: open-ended self-explanation with language-model feedback, menu-based self-explanation, and none at all. Every group improves over one fixed practice session, with no clear gap in post-test scores. On transfer problems, the open-ended group writes markedly better explanations for not-enough-information (NEI) items, gaining 11.9 percentage points over control. Those gains arrive even though the open-ended learners finish far fewer practice problems in the same time.
arxiv-2604-00242: Jarolím and Fajčík modify ColBERT retrieval to surface fine-grained relevance tokens, distilling signals from a large language model directly into the retrieval function. On MS MARCO, their 110M-parameter FGR-ColBERT reaches a token-level F1 of 64.5, beating Gemma 2 with 27 billion parameters at 62.8, despite being about 245 times smaller. Retrieval quality holds at 99 percent relative Recall at 50, and the system stays efficient with only a small latency overhead against the original ColBERT.
arxiv-2604-00542: Beňo and colleagues present an online predictive controller for CubeSat slews. It keeps star trackers in use while tracking ground targets. Nonlinear rigid body motion and shape limits are made linear around the current state estimate at each step. That yields a changing linear form cast as a standard quadratic program. The form fits space flight software practice and runs with lower online load than nonlinear rivals. It sets angular rate, actuator, and star tracker keep-out limits over a rolling horizon. Tests use NASA's 42 dynamics simulator.
arxiv-2604-00842: Nathani and colleagues introduce Pare, a test bed for proactive agents that guess user needs and act on their own in digital settings. Pare treats apps as finite state machines with state-aware navigation and state-based actions, making active user simulation possible. Its Pare-Bench benchmark spans 143 tasks across communication, productivity, scheduling, and lifestyle apps, testing goal inference, intervention timing, and multi-app orchestration.
arxiv-2604-01442: Vikram and Padhye ask whether coding agents can synthesize programs strong enough to replace coverage guidance and mutation in fuzzing. Gentoo gives an LLM coding agent shell access and source code. It instructs the agent to synthesize and refine a generator, with predicate-level test feedback. On fuzz targets for 7 Java libraries, agent-synthesized ones achieve higher coverage than human-written baselines on 4 of 7 benchmarks. Coverage guidance and mutation help human-written generators but not agent-synthesized ones. That suggests encoded logic in agent ones makes coverage guidance unnecessary.
arxiv-2604-01942: Adhikari, Alam and Johari model a family of lead-free antiperovskite compounds, Ba3MA3, as greener replacements for lead halide perovskites in light-based devices. First-principles calculations covering stability, excitons, polarons and device behavior find the cubic compounds stable in motion and heat, direct-gap semiconductors with gaps spanning 1.23 to 2.17 eV. Exciton binding stays moderate with mid-sized excitons, carrier-phonon coupling stays middling, and mobility runs high. Predicted efficiency ceilings beat several lead-based perovskites, marking the family a sturdy green platform.
arxiv-2604-02042: In their 2026 paper, Döhrer and Dohmen prove a Fenchel theorem for Gauss maps, giving sharp lower bounds for the path length of Gauss maps of an embedding. Combining that theorem with geometric analysis tools, they show circles minimize most generalized tangent-point energies. They further prove disks minimize all fractional Willmore energies among convex planar sets.
arxiv-2604-02442: Hu and colleagues make storage compute reversible with ReFlux on CXL SSDs. Static offload proves brittle: processors throttle under heat, and opaque vendor interfaces inflate adoption costs. ReFlux splits I/O logic into migratable WebAssembly actors, sharing state through CXL memory, moving only about 8 KB of control state. A thermal aware scheduler switches stages as heat or queue pressure rises, sending heavy actors to the host. Tests show over twice throttled device throughput under sustained writes, and far higher inference throughput under cache pressure.
arxiv-2604-02642: Meng and five colleagues test whether engagement with a social robot transfers into human-directed social skills for autistic children at home. In an 8-week trial with 40 children aged 5 to 9, continued robot access cut anxiety, confirming strong affective benefits. Yet children whose robot was withdrawn improved more in social motivation, emotion understanding and empathy toward caregivers and peers, showing engagement alone does not guarantee transfer.
arxiv-2604-02742: Huang and five colleagues propose TGPNet, a unified framework for restoring remote sensing images degraded in many ways at once. Most methods handle one degradation type in uniform data, but real scenes mix denoising, cloud and shadow removal, deblurring, and radar despeckling across spectral bands. Task-guided prompting uses learnable task embeddings to steer the decoder per degradation, keeping one shared weight set across RGB, multispectral, SAR, and thermal inputs.
arxiv-2604-02942: Islam presents the first machine learning analysis of NASA dataset OSD-970 on female mouse white adipose tissue after 37 days of microgravity aboard the International Space Station. Using gene expression data from 16 female mice, 8 flown and 8 ground controls, the team applies differential expression analysis and explainable AI. The analysis reveals a dramatic 12-fold upregulation of Ucp1 in microgravity-exposed tissue, with significant activation of the thermogenesis pathway. Random Forest led the classifiers tested.
arxiv-2604-03142: Wang and colleagues date the Kepler open cluster NGC 6866 by fitting isochrone clouds that vary the input physics, then checking the results against seismic ages. Gaia data yielded 180 members, and 19 gravity-mode pulsators gave a shared age of 759 million years, matching one isochrone set but not another. They conclude cluster ages hinge on assumed physics and mixing, so stellar models need better calibration.
arxiv-2604-03242: Wang and colleagues make agent safety auditing easier by splitting judgment into two learned stages instead of a single binary verdict. An Extractor compresses a long, noisy trajectory into a compact latent draft, and a Reasoner reads both draft and trajectory to predict safety. Accuracy rose from about 63 percent to about 91 percent across benchmarks, and ablations show the two stages work in synergy.
arxiv-2604-03442: Arakelian and Matevosyan prove in a 2026 note a direct twin of Hadamard's three-circle theorem for harmonic functions on non-concentric spheres. The result extends the concentric case to linked, non-touching spheres through a flip technique, measured in a weighted mean-square norm. Uses include spread of smallness and uniqueness results for harmonic functions.
arxiv-2604-03542: Michel and colleagues study 31 rural high school teachers across three US states to learn how AI shapes teaching in poorly funded rural schools. They find teachers use AI to streamline tasks. Yet poor resources, tech gaps, resistance to adoption, and missing AI know-how training block meaningful uptake. Teachers still hope AI can support them and their students, but findings call for rural-first design that narrows rather than widens barriers.
arxiv-2604-03742: Yulong He and colleagues improved how language models judge other models by breaking each verdict into clear criteria, rather than asking for one bare score. They used the Analytic Hierarchy Process to weigh those criteria, then added fuzzy numbers that carry how sure the judge is. Their DualJudge system blends a direct overall score with the structured breakdown, giving more weight to the side that hangs together best. Tested on JudgeBench, the structured methods beat direct scoring, and DualJudge came out on top overall.
arxiv-2604-03842: Mahesh Ramani worked out the spectrum of the toroidal three-dimensional queen graph, a graph on a torus grid where queens move as in chess. Fourier characters diagonalize its adjacency matrix, giving eigenvalues from a count of queen directions orthogonal to each frequency. For generic odd n, that count takes only the values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, and 13. Each value comes with an explicit polynomial multiplicity, telling how often it occurs. A geometric classification plus two counting identities drives the proof.
arxiv-2604-04042: Konstanze Zwintz and team laid out the PLATO mission's science calibration and validation plan for its first long-pointing field, LOPS2 in the southern sky. The plan selects reference stars for the input catalogue, led by tens of thousands of red giants and thousands of early F-type gravity-mode pulsators. Their asteroseismic data will sharpen models of dwarf and subgiant interiors. The toughest demand is dating exoplanet host stars to better than 10 percent for a Sun-like star, a bar current models cannot yet clear for large samples.
arxiv-2604-04142: Liyu Zhang and team presented OP-GRPO, the first off-policy GRPO framework for flow-matching models. Standard GRPO trains on-policy and wastes samples, so OP-GRPO reuses high-quality trajectories from a replay buffer. A sequence-level importance-sampling correction keeps GRPO's clipping mechanism intact under off-policy data, and late denoising steps are truncated to avoid ill-conditioned ratios. Across image and video benchmarks, it matched or beat Flow-GRPO with only 34.2 percent of the training steps on average.
arxiv-2604-04342: Cheng, Zhu and Xie present a tutorial on generative models for choices when live data drifts from past data. Flow- and score-based models matter less for making samples than for shaping and shifting distributions through transport maps, velocity fields and score fields. Their shared frame rests on pushforward maps, continuity, Fokker-Planck equations, Wasserstein geometry and probability-space tuning. Within it, models learn baseline doubt, build stressed distributions, and yield conditional distributions under partial data. The tutorial notes promises on flow convergence and minimax analysis.
arxiv-2604-04442: Zhang, Goel and Ahmad present the Causal Multi-Agent Decision Framework for cyber defense, mixing causal models with adversarial dual-policy control. Current defense lines lean on link signals, lack firm limits and drift under hostile inputs. C-MADF learns a structural causal model from past telemetry, built into a directed acyclic graph setting admissible transitions. A dual-agent system pits a threat-tuned Blue-Team policy against a cautious Red-Team policy. On CICIoT2023, C-MADF cuts the false-positive rate to 1.8 percent, well below three past baselines.
arxiv-2604-04642: Wang and six colleagues present WaterSplat-SLAM, a monocular underwater SLAM system with robust pose estimation and photorealistic mapping. Underwater monocular SLAM serves robot underwater vehicles and marine archaeology, yet methods struggle to produce sharp maps. The system couples meaning-based medium filter into two-view 3D reconstruction before tracking and depth gauging. It also uses guided rendering and live map handling with an online medium-aware Gaussian map, shaping the scene in a lifelike and compact way. Experiments on many underwater sets show tracking and high-fidelity rendering.
arxiv-2604-04742: Gurses and Sichitiu propose ACHEM, the first software-based wireless channel emulation environment for software-defined radios. Digital twins are becoming a tool for next-generation wireless systems. Yet no general-purpose testing environment exists for software-defined-radio-based systems. With ACHEM, any software-radio-based system can be fully emulated in a pure digital environment without specialized hardware. The emulator supports multiple transmitters and receivers, MIMO communications and multiple frequencies. ACHEM is validated with GNU Radio, srsRAN 4G/5G and OpenAirInterface.
arxiv-2604-04842: Xu and nine colleagues test whether chatbots used in mental health care can be tricked into harmful support. Their attack method, PCSA, plays a steady fictional client whose persona steers multi-turn talks toward unsafe ground. It exposes a gap between genuine empathy and validation that reinforces risky beliefs. Across seven general and specialist models, the method beat four rival attacks, and the tested systems gave unlicensed medical advice, backed delusions, and nudged risky acts.
arxiv-2604-05142: Harris builds a model of evolution for AIs, where traits spread through the success of earlier systems in designing descendants. Unlike evolution, where DNA changes are random, AI self-design is strongly directed. He replaces a random walk of mutations with a directed tree of possible designs, while humans control the fitness function allocating resources. Fitness may not rise, but with bounded fitness and an eta-locking condition, it concentrates on the maximum value. If fooling human evaluators adds to fitness, evolution selects for both capability and deception.
arxiv-2604-05242: Xu and three colleagues propose XMark, a method for hiding and reading notes in LLM texts. Marking embeds binary notes into text, giving credit and tracing of bad use. Old methods: some grow too big for notes, others trade quality against scores, and scores drop when texts have few tokens. The encoder gives a bent logit spread, keeping quality, while its decoder reads notes with few tokens. Across tasks, XMark lifts reading scores while keeping text quality, beating prior methods.
arxiv-2604-05542: Hsiao, Huang, and Li localize Bergman kernels for unbounded pseudoconvex domains near finite-type boundary points, settling a question open since Engliš treated bounded domains decades ago. Combined with a Mir-Zaitsev extension result, they show a bounded real-analytic domain's Bergman metric is Einstein only for the unit ball. The work advances the Cheng-Yau conjecture and links microlocal analysis with complex geometry.
arxiv-2604-05942: Ghaddar, Kobyzev, Chen, and Cui offer BOSCH, a training-free way to pick which attention heads in a language model should swap full attention for short sliding windows, cutting KV cache use. Layer probes first rank layer sensitivity, then each layer gets its own short-window share, and heads are tuned in groups within share bands. On four models from 1.7B to 30B parameters, BOSCH beats layer rules and six static head methods, with bigger wins at high short-window shares.
arxiv-2604-06042: Ranhili and colleagues' 2026 study uses resonant inelastic X-ray scattering to find signs of spin-phonon coupling in CrSBr, where magnetism meets lattice vibration. Low-energy excitations appear only in the cold antiferromagnetic phase, including a quasi-elastic peak near 42 meV under pi polarization. Calculations link these features to bond-bending optical phonon modes in the chromium-sulfur-chromium network. Their fading on warming, plus polarization dependence and modelling, points to magnetic order strongly shaping phonon-related spectral weight rather than purely lattice effects.
arxiv-2604-06242: Fang completes a proof of a conjecture on double Lambert series parity, from Andrews, Dixit, Schultz, and Yee. In 2026, Amdeberhan, Andrews, and Ballantine published ideas pointing toward the proof, leaving part of the argument open. Fang's paper finishes the remaining steps, closing the gap their work left. The result settles the conjectured parity claim in full.
arxiv-2604-06742: Hu and four colleagues test whether language models can build command-line tools from scratch. Older benchmarks hand models structural scaffolds, reducing the job to file filling, or grade with rigid white-box unit tests that force specific internals. Their CLI-Tool-Bench gives agents an empty workspace across 94 real repositories and grades finished tools by black-box differential testing against human-written oracles. Seven leading models were tried, and the best reached under 44 percent overall success, with agents tending toward monolithic code and extra tokens buying no better results.
arxiv-2604-06942: Calderon, Johansson, and Günlü test post-quantum key schemes with deep-learning tests. Ciphertext indistinguishability underpins cryptographic security, but validating it in hybrid systems is hard. Modeling IND-CPA games as binary classification with labeled ciphertext data, they train neural distinguishers on schemes behind ML-KEM, BIKE, and HQC. They also test hybrid combiners with RSA variants and plaintext, and cascade symmetric encryption with AES, ChaCha20, and DES variants. No algorithm or combination shows a significant edge, matching theory that hybrids with one secure component stay indistinguishable.
arxiv-2604-07642: Zhao and two colleagues fully resolve the Gyori, Salia and Zamora problem on Berge-Turan extremal numbers. They prove the extremal number for connected r-uniform hypergraphs with no Berge path of length k-1 holds for k at least 2r+2, failing below, improving on 2r+14. They improve Furedi, Kostochka and Luo on 2-connected hypergraphs with no Berge cycle of k or more, showing the same threshold, improving on 4r. Their approach reduces Berge-Turan problems to extremal graph theory, applying work on feasibility and the Kelmans operation.
arxiv-2604-07842: Luo studies how higher-order interactions reshape chaotic responses in systems with active amplitudes. Phase coherence alone does not fix group instability. His minimal model couples four nonisochronous Stuart-Landau oscillators globally, with pairwise and symmetric three-body links. The pairwise system already supports a chaotic branch, so the higher-order channel reshapes irregular motion instead of making it. That reshaping follows effective-frequency shear more closely than alignment: coupling evens out size differences, uneven timing turns them into varied spin rates, and the shear shapes the Lyapunov response.
arxiv-2604-07942: Qian, Wang, Mohanty, and Chen offer a scalable frequentist method for detecting continuous gravitational waves in pulsar timing array data. Bayesian methods grow costly fast, since noise and signal counts multiply with array size, limiting future arrays of hundreds of pulsars. Their method pairs an adaptive spline fitting step that suppresses red noise without parametric models against a scheme for choosing which pulsar subsets enter the analysis. Skipping complex noise models keeps computation manageable while preserving detection power for large arrays.
arxiv-2604-08342: Tang and five colleagues present EgoEverything, a benchmark for behavior-inspired long context first-person video understanding. Long context first-person video work draws significant focus, with augmented reality among top application domains. The task stays hard, needing reasoning over long contexts and unstructured activities. Although several benchmarks exist, most first-person datasets use worn cameras and focus on visual content, barely weighing user conduct in queries. EgoEverything considers human conduct using gaze-derived attention signals for questions. It holds over 5,000 questions.
arxiv-2604-08442: Cultra, Yin, Bartlett, and Porporato model how soil moisture and plants steer moist convection and rainfall over land. In their stochastic model, convective energy depends on soil wetness through surface fluxes and boundary layer growth, with loamy sand favoring storms at higher wetness than sandy or clay rich soils. Plant water strategies further shape drying, and rainfall feedback can lock soils into lasting wet or dry regimes.
arxiv-2604-08642: Khovanskii proves a necessary condition for solving algebraic equations by radicals, using Galois theory. Written as a handout for a Toronto course on polynomial equations and fields, the note reviews the needed Galois results from class and applies textbook results without reproving them. The matching sufficient condition, based on linear algebra, is promised for the next handout.
arxiv-2604-08842: Agarwal and three colleagues test CAAP, an unusual method for gauging the current growth speed of coronal mass bursts from single point in situ readings. Radial lineup of Solar Orbiter and Wind during 3 to 5 November 2021 gives joint views of a magnet cloud center and trailing edge. That gives a direct measure of growth speed to check against CAAP guesses at both craft. The team also tracks shock, sheath, and magnet cloud parts, finding a stronger shock at Wind, near constant sheath thickness, and rising flux that breaks flux saving.
arxiv-2604-08942: Gniewek studies budding yeast cell packings after jamming, when not every bud is mechanically pinned down. Gniewek builds a mean-field theory in two variables: pressure and the share of buds still free. It shows that stress feedback slows growth on loaded buds and redirects it to free ones. As free buds finish, they add contacts that raise coordination and rigidity with little extra pressure, so feedback-driven growth becomes its own stiffening mechanism.
arxiv-2604-09042: Helled and six colleagues review disk instability as a way giant planets form. The model helps explain giants that form early, giants far from their stars, and giants around small M-type stars, cases that challenge rival accounts. The review covers recent hydrodynamical and magneto-hydrodynamical disk models, population synthesis models, and models of clump collisions. It also covers new observations of such systems.
arxiv-2604-09542: Lee, Cho, and Seo build effective U(2) Chern-Simons-Ginzburg-Landau theories for fractional quantum Hall hierarchies, both Abelian and non-Abelian, that previously lived only as categorical data or trial wavefunctions. Their framework covers Abelian hierarchies built on half-filled Pfaffian-type parents and non-Abelian ones growing from Abelian states. It reproduces every filling fraction from wavefunction and categorical constructions and, more strongly, pins down each corresponding topological order. A particle-hole symmetry also emerges, linking two hierarchy sequences that generate the Read-Rezayi states and their conjugates.
arxiv-2604-09842: Lyons and Wickramaratne show that DX behavior limits n-type carriers in ultrawide-bandgap nitrides like aluminum nitride and cubic boron nitride. Instead of acting as donors, DX centers trap two electrons, holding a negative charge state. Silicon dopes n-type best here, with its aluminum nitride DX level about 270 millielectronvolts from the band minimum. Many silicon impurities in aluminum nitride will be negatively charged and compensate the n-type doping. Density functional theory shows compensation in silicon-doped aluminum nitride, even without any other defects.
arxiv-2604-09942: Tartaglini and Lepori test whether vision models bind objects using Gestalt flow, beyond likeness and nearness. Binding joins low-level cues into object pictures, a long-standing challenge for neural networks. Using made sets, they show binding probes respond to flow across many ready vision models, and find certain focus heads tracking flow that carry over across sets. Cutting those heads shows they often help build pictures holding object binding.
arxiv-2604-10742: Feng, Li, and Kurths model an SIRS epidemic on a birth-death evolving network, where nodes appear and vanish over time. Unlike most studies that treat network change as slower than disease spread, they let disease and networks co-evolve. Their network adds nodes and deletes some by heredity, capturing migration and indirect contacts during an outbreak. A Markovian queueing network tracks group sizes across disease states, and tests show migration and indirect contacts shift those groups, with new indirect contacts aiding spread.
arxiv-2604-10842: Agyemang and colleagues present Resilient Write, an MCP server putting a six-layer tough write layer between agents and the file system. When a write fails from filters, cuts, or dropped sessions, agents get no clear signal, lose the draft, and burn tokens retrying blind. The six layers, early risk scores, atomic writes, safe resume chunking, typed errors, scratchpad storage, and task handoff notes, stand alone and work singly. A 186-test suite checks each layer, showing a 5 times faster recovery and a 13 times better agent self-fix rate.
arxiv-2604-11342: Tähtinen, Asikainen, and Mursula speed up solar dipole simulations with a dipole flux transport matrix method. Instead of running a full surface flux transport model, they evolve basis vectors of a synoptic map and compress the resulting propagator matrices to under one ten-thousandth of their original size. The method runs 100 to 1000 times faster than a four-year simulation of a single active region, and 80 times faster on solar cycle 24 within 1 percent agreement. Thousands of runs now fit in minutes on a basic laptop.
arxiv-2604-11642: Drobchik and Khaibrakhmanov analyze gravitational stability across 1,155 protoplanetary disks from ten surveys of star-forming regions. Disk masses follow a power law with index 1.36 plus or minus 0.14. Computing the Toomre parameter for each disk under a power-law radial density profile, they find only 1.2 percent formally unstable and 1.7 percent marginally stable. The scarcity of unstable disks contradicts theory and may reflect systematic mass underestimation from observational limits. Accounting for optical depth, CO depletion, and gas-to-dust uncertainty, they conclude truly unstable systems may be significantly more common.
arxiv-2604-11742: Zhan and five colleagues study discourse diversity in empathic dialogue. LLMs give empathic one-turn responses yet reuse lexical patterns. Less studied is whether formulaicity extends to discourse moves, what responses do. Prior work shows LLMs reuse tactic sequences more than humans. In multi-turn talks, rigidity compounds: once a tactic appears, LLMs reuse it next at fifty to fifty-six hundredths, versus twenty-seven hundredths for humans. This holds across LLMs in real talks, invisible to standard metrics. They introduce MINT, a reinforcement learning framework boosting discourse diversity.
arxiv-2604-11842: Chen and eight colleagues introduce DBGL, a method for sorting irregular medical time series where sampling rates differ, readings arrive out of sync, and gaps vary. A patient-variable bipartite graph captures sampling patterns without forced lining up and models links between variables, while a per-node decay code tracks fading with sampling interval. Tested on four public datasets, DBGL outperforms all baselines.
arxiv-2604-11942: Kakimoto and twelve colleagues study how small-scale surroundings quench massive galaxies between redshifts 1 and 5. They spectroscopically confirm a galaxy group tied to a massive quiescent galaxy at redshift 4.53, with at least three star-forming galaxies within 150 proper kiloparsecs. In the COSMOS field, the quiescent fraction runs higher in overdensities than in the field, especially near 200 proper kiloparsecs. Environmental dependence weakens beyond redshift 3 overall, yet persists for the most massive galaxies, suggesting accelerated evolution in dense regions began early.
arxiv-2604-12042: Murphy proves necessary and sufficient conditions for a Hilbert-space-valued function to admit a Karhunen-Loève-type eigenfunction series. The classical form already exists for certain square-integrable stochastic elements. It is widely used in time series and signal processing. Drawing on Bochner and Hilbert-Schmidt space theory, he builds an isomorphism between those spaces and shows it is natural. An example shows the computing gains of the wider setting.
arxiv-2604-12342: Li and three colleagues show subset training is not privacy free: choosing which data to include or exclude creates its own privacy surface. Their CoLA framework studies leakage through side-channel metadata and through model outputs, defining subset-aware side-channel attacks and black-box attacks. Two surfaces matter: training-membership inference for training data alone, and selection-participation inference covering every sample in the selection process. Tests on vision and language models show existing threat models underestimate the risk.
arxiv-2604-12542: Laura Boca de Giuli and six colleagues make predictive control learn safely while running. Predictive control must gather fresh data without breaking safety or quality. Their scheme updates only the last layer of a recurrent neural network, using Bayesian learning. Learning alternates between exploration and goal-reaching phases.
